big_idea: Sort 2D shapes by SIDES + SYMMETRY: count edges, fold to test symmetry.
learning_intention: We are learning to sort shapes by sides, angles, and symmetry.
student_learning_goal: I can sort shapes by sides, angles, and symmetry.
success_criteria: I can FIND lines of symmetry.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Symmy and Flippy — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Symmy: This SQUARE has 4 sides, 4 angles, and 4 lines of symmetry! Let's count them all! Symmy opens: 'Count the SIDES — fold the SHAPE — match the HALVES!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Symmy and Flippy puppets. 'Friends — I'm Symmy the Symmetry Squirrel and this is Flippy the Folding Frog. Today we sort shapes by THREE things: SIDES, ANGLES, and LINES OF SYMMETRY.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write SIDE, ANGLE, SYMMETRY LINE on chart. 'Side = a straight edge. Angle = a corner where 2 sides meet. Symmetry line = a line that splits a shape into matching halves.'

Demonstrate with a square. Hold one up. 'Count sides: 1, 2, 3, 4 — FOUR SIDES.' Trace each side. 'Count angles: 1, 2, 3, 4 — FOUR ANGLES.' Touch each corner. Now fold the square in half — 'MATCH! 1 line of symmetry.' Fold differently — 'Match again! 2 lines.' Diagonal — 'Match! 3 lines.' Other diagonal — 'Match! 4 lines.' 'A square has FOUR lines of symmetry.'

More examples:
- Triangle (equilateral): 3 sides, 3 angles, 3 lines of symmetry.
- Rectangle: 4 sides, 4 angles, 2 lines of symmetry.
- Circle: 0 sides, 0 angles, INFINITE lines of symmetry.
- Hexagon (regular): 6 sides, 6 angles, 6 lines of symmetry.
- Letter L: 6 sides, 6 angles, 0 lines of symmetry.
- Heart: many sides, no straight angles, 1 line of symmetry.

'Symmy says — count THREE things for every shape. Now we sort by ANY of the three.'

'Today we sort 30 shapes 3 ways.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: count sides/angles/symmetry on 4 shapes.
Three stations. A: Sort 30 shapes by NUMBER OF SIDES. B: Sort by NUMBER OF SYMMETRY LINES. C: Pick attribute and sort.
Stretch at C: 2-attribute sort (4-sided AND symmetric).
Discuss: same shape, different sorting attribute = different piles.
steps.teacher_prompt: Show: square has 4 sides, but also has 4 lines of symmetry. Sorts in different categories.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their fold-test methods. Class debates folding vs drawing-the-line and checking both halves match. Cite Battista (2007) — geometric reasoning requires multiple verification methods.
steps.teacher_prompt: Symmy: 'Two paths to symmetry. The MATH says: halves must MATCH.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at A. Sort by sides only.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children form shape outlines with their bodies; count sides physically.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: counts sides; counts angles; finds symmetry lines.

discussion_prompts: How many lines does a SQUARE have?
Symmy's preview: tomorrow Flippy REARRANGES these shapes — but watch what stays the SAME (Lesson 2 — E1.2 area conservation).
consolidation.exit_routine: Symmy's refrain — class chants: 'Count the SIDES — fold the SHAPE — match the HALVES!' (3x). Each child writes one shape with side-count + symmetry verdict.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 1 surfaces children who can count attributes.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child counts CORNERS as SIDES — repairing the corner-side mix-up at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On 'sort shapes by sides + symmetry', the dominant Grade-2 trap is geometric attribute confusion (Battista 2007; Clements & Sarama 2009): child conflates side-count with symmetry, or names corners instead of sides. Without precise attribute naming, Lesson 2's decomposition and Lesson 3's congruence cannot ground.

Today: name attributes precisely; test symmetry by folding. Tomorrow Lesson 2 decomposes/conserves area; Lesson 3 congruence; Lesson 4 maps; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair at Station A. Child looks at a square, says '8' (counting both 4 sides and 4 corners as same attribute).
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You said 8. Symmy asks — sides are STRAIGHT LINES. Corners are POINTS. Count just the sides.'

Guide. 'Trace each STRAIGHT LINE: 1, 2, 3, 4. Stop. Now count CORNERS: 1, 2, 3, 4. They're DIFFERENT.'

Generlise. 'Symmy says — sides are EDGES. Angles are CORNERS where 2 edges meet. Count them separately.'

If still confused: provide a shape with sides numbered 1-4 in colour and corners numbered 1-4 in different colour.
expected_student_responses: (Stretched) Notices regular shapes have side count = angle count = symmetry count.
common_misconceptions: Sides = corners. (Repair: sides are EDGES, corners are POINTS.)
Symmetry lines = sides. (Repair: symmetry lines split the shape.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child conflates sides + corners: drill 'count EDGES, not corners'; child traces one edge at a time.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child sorts by symmetry but won't fold-check: force the fold-and-match test before any sort decision.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can fold but misses asymmetry: explicit rule 'if halves don't EXACTLY match, NOT symmetric.'

parts_outline.task: Find lines of symmetry for 4 shapes.
Sort 6 shapes by number of sides.
